Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: No authoritative, specific requirement for mandatory personal-data breach notification was found in reviewed official or legal sources; searches focused on Algeria Law 18-07 breach notification, cybersecurity incident reporting, and payment security incident reporting but did not yield clear mandatory notification provisions.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A single light-touch search surfaced clearly authoritative sources, so this row was escalated from the fast path to the full path. DLA Piper's Data Protection Laws of the World (Algeria, breach notification page, last modified 20 Jan 2025) confirms that Law No. 18-07 requires service providers to notify the national data protection authority and affected data subjects 'without delay' of a personal-data breach, with criminal sanctions for non-compliance. Law No. 25-11 of 24 July 2025, which amends Law 18-07, adds a specific 5-day notification deadline to the ANPDP. Bank of Algeria Règlement 25-02 (2025) confirms that licensed payment service providers are explicitly subject to Law 18-07/25-11 data-protection obligations. This is a legally mandated requirement, so the score is revised from 0 (Unknown) to 3 (Mandatory).
revised_comments: Algeria's data protection law (Law No. 18-07 of 2018, as amended by Law No. 25-11 of 24 July 2025) imposes a mandatory personal-data breach notification requirement on data controllers and service providers, including payment service providers, which are explicitly brought within the scope of the data protection regime by Bank of Algeria Règlement 25-02. Controllers must notify the National Authority for the Protection of Personal Data (ANPDP) within five days of becoming aware of a breach and must notify affected data subjects without delay where the breach may affect their privacy. Non-compliance carries administrative sanctions, including fines and suspension or withdrawal of authorisation, and criminal penalties of up to ten years' imprisonment and fines of up to DZD 10,000,000.

Definition: Whether the scheme rules governing payment system participation, pricing structure, technical requirements, security standards, and conduct are publicly accessible via website, public repository, or on request. Transparency indicator.
Comments: No official publicly accessible “scheme rulebook” for the instant payment/mobile switch or interbank payment scheme was located in sources reviewed (Bank of Algeria pages reviewed describe oversight, but do not publish scheme rules).

revision_notes: A light-touch search surfaced Bank of Algeria Règlement 25-02 (2025) and Instruction 06-2025 (17 Aug 2025), published regulatory instruments covering PSP licensing, governance, technical, security and consumer-conduct requirements, reportedly issued via the Official Gazette. However, these are general central-bank regulations for payment service providers rather than a dedicated 'scheme rulebook' for the national interbank/instant-payment switch (SATIM/CPI) as the variable's definition and original comments envisage, and the primary Journal Officiel text or a SATIM-published rulebook could not be directly verified. It is unclear whether general PSP regulation satisfies the 'scheme rules' definition, so this is flagged for human review rather than assigning a guessed score.
revised_comments: Bank of Algeria Règlement 25-02 and Instruction 06-2025 establish published regulatory requirements for payment service provider licensing, governance, technical and security standards, and consumer protection, issued via the Official Gazette. No dedicated, publicly accessible scheme rulebook specific to the national interbank payment switch has been identified.

Definition: Whether independent external audits of payment system security, operations, financial controls, and compliance are conducted by third-party auditors, and whether audit results or summaries are made public.
Comments: No clear, public independent audit/review of the national payment switch/instant payment scheme (e.g., SATIM/CPI) was identified in accessible sources reviewed; searches focused on SATIM annual report/audit, CPI audit, payment system external review.

revision_notes: A light-touch search found that Bank of Algeria Règlement 25-02 reportedly requires licensed payment service providers' annual financial statements to be certified by an external auditor (commissaire aux comptes), with the appointment subject to prior approval by the banking commission — suggesting a private, non-public audit requirement. However, this was sourced from a secondary compliance-training website (Beeform Academy) paraphrasing the regulation rather than the primary Journal Officiel text, and it pertains to PSP financial-statement audits rather than a security/operational audit of the national payment switch (SATIM/CPI) that the variable specifically asks about. Given reliance on a single non-primary source and the narrower scope of the evidence, this is flagged for human review rather than confidently upgraded from Unknown.
revised_comments: Bank of Algeria Règlement 25-02 reportedly requires licensed payment service providers to have their annual financial statements certified by an external auditor, with the auditor's appointment subject to prior approval by the banking commission. No evidence of publicly disclosed audit or security-review results for the national payment switch (SATIM/CPI) has been identified.

Definition: Percentage of government payments (G2P disbursements including salaries, pensions, social transfers) made through instant digital payment system rather than cash or check, reflecting government adoption and modernization.
Comments: No quantified, nationwide estimate of the share of total government payments digitized was found in reviewed sources; evidence only indicates specific programs such as student scholarships paid into bank accounts, but not enough to score overall government payment digitization on the requested 0–5 scale.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: A light-touch search surfaced substantive but non-quantified evidence — the AADL 3 housing programme mandating digital-only payment of housing instalments (3.6 million transactions worth 65.27 billion DZD in December 2025 alone), and a pilot digital portal for National Solidarity sector benefits including the Lump Sum Solidarity Allowance, launched in two municipalities from March 2026 — prompting escalation to the full path. However, AADL 3 instalments are citizen-to-government (P2G) payments, not G2P disbursements, and the National Solidarity portal is a registration/enrolment pilot in only two municipalities, not evidence of nationwide G2P payment digitisation. No aggregate percentage of government-to-person disbursements (salaries, pensions, social transfers) made digitally could be found, so the 0/Unknown score is confirmed rather than upgraded.
revised_comments: No consolidated, quantified estimate of the share of total government-to-person payments (salaries, pensions, social transfers) disbursed digitally in Algeria is publicly available. Discrete digitisation initiatives are under way, including a pilot digital portal for National Solidarity sector benefits launched in two municipalities in March 2026, but these do not yet provide a basis for a nationwide estimate.
